overview: Cyclone Arnab nears the Andhra and Odisha coast, Israel votes today, the BJP-Congress row over Kharge's remark continues, and the rupee stays near 95 to the dollar.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab nears the Andhra and Odisha coast
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha are on alert as Cyclone Arnab moves toward land.
items.detail: Reports say the storm has turned 'very severe', with heavy rain likely in Andhra and Yanam, and trains cancelled. Schools in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands were shut through Tuesday, and some Odisha districts have closures on 28 and 29 October.

items.headline: Israelis vote in a tight election as Netanyahu touts Trump's backing
items.summary: Israel holds its election on Tuesday, with Netanyahu campaigning on Trump's endorsement.
items.detail: Reuters reports that Netanyahu has suggested the two could restart the war on Iran, and Al Jazeera has gathered the leading candidates' views on the main issues. Netanyahu's main opponent is reported to agree with him on Israel's security.

items.headline: Five shot dead at a Guwahati hotel after owner-leaseholder dispute
items.summary: Five people were shot dead at a hotel in Guwahati after a dispute between the owner and a leaseholder.
items.detail: Reports say four of the dead were from the same family. The accused has been arrested, according to The Times of India.

items.headline: Egypt's parliament backs military support for Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Egypt's parliament has authorised military aid for Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate.
items.detail: The vote lets President el-Sisi act to defend Saudi Arabia, and some outlets say it risks drawing Houthi fire. In the same week, Saudi forces reported intercepting a Houthi ballistic missile and drones near Riyadh's airport, which has partly reopened.

items.headline: Kharge remark row: BJP protests spread, Congress hits back
items.summary: BJP workers protested in several cities over Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's remark about PM Modi. Congress says Modi is playing the victim.
items.detail: The BJP wants an apology, and some groups are demanding Kharge's resignation. In Shimla, protesters clashed with police during an effigy-burning attempt. Congress says Modi sought votes in his mother's name and that Kharge is one of the most senior leaders, so his words should be read in that light.

items.headline: Election Commission tells Supreme Court SIR decisions were unanimous
items.summary: The Election Commission says all its SIR orders were unanimous and Form 6 was not amended.
items.detail: The affidavit responds to a challenge against the ECI, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR decisions. The ECI also says the CEC can be removed only as a Supreme Court judge can. The Supreme Court has said no action should be taken on deleted voters using Form 6, and the hearing continued on Tuesday.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi acquitted in 2018 defamation case
items.summary: A court has acquitted Congress leader and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi in a defamation case over 2018 remarks.
items.detail: Congress has criticised the BJP over the tone of political debate after the verdict. Rahul Gandhi is due to hold a rally in Delhi on 1 November, and he said the BJP had helped promote it.

items.headline: Great Nicobar power plant moves a step closer with NTPC site-works tender
items.summary: A 108 MW gas engine power plant planned for Great Nicobar has moved closer to implementation, with NTPC tendering site-enabling works.
items.detail: The report from Campbell Bay describes the tender as a step toward the plant. Separately, commercial LPG consumers on the island are being charged an extra ₹1,229.92 per 19 kg cylinder for transport. The Great Nicobar project is a large integrated development that has drawn environmental and tribal-rights objections.
items.why_it_matters: This is a concrete procurement step on the project you follow closely; no new court or clearance news appeared today.

items.headline: UNESCO adds Andaman volcanic landscapes to tentative list
items.summary: UNESCO has added Andaman volcanic landscapes to its tentative list, along with Chhattisgarh temples.
items.detail: A tentative list entry is the first formal step before a site can be nominated for World Heritage status. The Andaman entry is one of three new Indian sites announced in this update.
items.why_it_matters: It is a rare piece of positive Andaman news and could eventually bring more attention to the islands' conservation.

items.headline: India's green cover falls from 36.9% in 2001 to 31.35% in 2025, study finds
items.summary: A new study reports that India's green cover shrank from 36.9% in 2001 to 31.35% in 2025.
items.detail: The figures come as India debates compensatory afforestation, the system where forest loss is offset by planting elsewhere, and a new policy review questions how well that works. Green cover figures depend on satellite assessments and how forest is defined.
items.why_it_matters: It gives long-term context to the forest and land debates around the Great Nicobar project.

sources.name: IMPRI Impact and Policy Research Institute

items.headline: XN Global acquires Morgan Price's international health insurance portfolio
items.summary: XN Global has acquired Morgan Price's international health insurance portfolio, expanding its IPMI business.
items.detail: The deal is reported to leave existing policyholder benefits and broker servicing arrangements unchanged. Portfolio transfers like this are common in the IPMI market, and they can change which entity brokers deal with on policy servicing.
items.why_it_matters: A change of carrier in the IPMI market can affect broker relationships, so it is worth checking which entity handles your partners' accounts.

items.headline: Kerala plans a Bill to regulate high private hospital costs
items.summary: Kerala plans to bring a Bill in the next session to curb high treatment costs in private hospitals.
items.detail: The plan comes amid foreign-backed stakes in private hospitals, and the government is also pursuing a statewide health transformation and early-detection programme. Leader of Opposition Vijayan has accused the UDF government of trying to 'sabotage' the health sector through a wellness task force.
items.why_it_matters: You plan to return to Kerala, so rules on private hospital pricing there could shape your family's care costs and your insurance planning.

items.headline: Saudi flight cancellations continue even as Riyadh airport partly reopens
items.summary: Air India and Air India Express have cancelled Riyadh and Dammam flights until 7 November.
items.detail: Riyadh's airport has partly reopened, but cancellations on Saudi routes continue. Telegraph India reports that Houthi attacks have grounded about 7,800 departures and that Riyadh cancellations reached 86%. Keralites in Saudi Arabia are seeking affordable chartered flights.
items.why_it_matters: If you or your family travel to Saudi Arabia or connect through Riyadh, check flight status before you leave.

items.headline: Income-tax department nudges UAE property owners to disclose assets before 31 December
items.summary: The Income-tax department is contacting taxpayers with UAE properties to disclose undeclared foreign assets before the 31 December deadline.
items.detail: The department has sent reminders to owners who may not have declared their property. Under India's foreign asset disclosure rules, residents must report overseas holdings, including Dubai property, in their tax returns. A Times of India piece also calls for the government to come clean on UAE assets.
items.why_it_matters: If you own property in Dubai or hold other foreign assets, check that they are in your Indian return before the deadline.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty snap four-day losing streak
items.summary: Indian benchmarks rose on Monday as value buyers picked up beaten-down stocks.
items.detail: Sensex gained roughly 480 to 500 points, depending on the report, and Nifty closed above 22,750. Pharma and metal stocks led the recovery. The rebound followed four straight sessions of losses, and markets remain sensitive to oil prices and Middle East tensions.

items.headline: GIFT Nifty points to a weak start as crude stays high
items.summary: GIFT Nifty was about 110 points lower, near 22,663, in early trade on Tuesday.
items.detail: Reports put Brent crude around $110 to $115 a barrel, and Middle East tensions and the Fed decision are being watched. Some reports also show Asian markets turning higher, so the global picture is mixed.
items.why_it_matters: High crude feeds into India's inflation and the rupee, both of which affect your remittances and your ETF returns.

items.headline: Rupee closes at 95.22 to the dollar on oil-linked losses
items.summary: The rupee fell 29 paise to close at 95.22 against the dollar on Monday.
items.detail: It lost 84 paise over three sessions. Importers stepped up dollar bids and foreign outflows added pressure. Analysts say the rupee's oil-linked losses are meeting a key hurdle, with the RBI defending the currency.
items.why_it_matters: The dirham is pegged to the dollar, so the rupee's move against the dollar also changes the rupee-dirham rate you get when sending money home.

items.headline: Humans may have cancelled the next ice age
items.summary: A study published in Science argues that greenhouse warming stopped a natural slide toward another ice age.
items.detail: Researchers studying Arctic ice, including Canada's Barnes Ice Cap, say the ice had been expanding for at least 1,000 years before peaking around 1960. Greenhouse warming then reversed that natural trend.

items.headline: Penguin droppings may speed up snowmelt in Antarctica
items.summary: Penguin droppings appear to feed green algae that darken Antarctic snow, which may speed up melting.
items.detail: Studies linking the droppings to green snow algae suggest that nutrients from penguin colonies could be darkening the snow surface. Darker snow absorbs more sunlight and melts faster.

items.headline: Bengaluru's grease hunters want leftover fryer oil to fuel India's jets
items.summary: A group in Bengaluru is collecting used cooking oil as a feedstock for aviation fuel.
items.detail: Used cooking oil can be processed into sustainable aviation fuel, which is one way to reduce the emissions from flying. The Bloomberg piece highlights how waste collection is part of the supply chain.
items.why_it_matters: It is a small, practical climate idea that could matter for the air travel you take between Dubai and Kerala.
